findings.reason: a builder taking the bullet at face value will measure and optimise the fixed-point solve while the per-step all-node fit and Bell-field rebuild stay in place, and clause (2) then fails against a cost the plan asserted was already conditional; the plan should either name those two stages as per-step costs the section must remove or make the fit genuinely cell-selective.
findings.text: bullet 1 says the cell-local fit is paid "only in the cells that hold the tracked axis and X-point and the cells a Newton iterate enters" and that "Only a rebuild step pays for the fit over every node", but the read the section wires in (support_read.read) computes an own-node quadratic fit over every node on every call: `sampled_coefficient` (fixed_points.py:168-175) is invoked unconditionally by `read_at_stationary_points` (topology.py:3193), and `field_from_jets` (fixed_points.py:178-212) rebuilds the whole-mesh Bell coefficients from the nodal jets on every `support_read.read` (`support_read.py:108-112`) — neither is gated on a tracked point leaving its cell, so the all-node cost the bullet says a steady-state step avoids is in fact paid each step; the 0.2 ms clause (2) is therefore judged against a mechanism the cited implementation does not provide.

findings.reason: the claim's purpose is to establish that the read is unwired from the production route, which is true; a test caller does not alter the wiring decision or the section's work.
findings.text: the intro states "Nothing calls it, though", but `support_read.read_and_book` is exercised by `tests/test_support_read.py:51`, so the true statement is that no production route calls it.
